ingredients.h2: One plant, and three plants called bugle
ingredients.intro: A one ingredient list is a short section, and this one needs a paragraph about the name before anything else. Here is the plant the listing names, the plants it is not, the row the label leaves empty, and the shell.

cards.alt: Bark and root pieces at the edge of a painted nebula
cards.p: A square stemmed perennial of wet ground in eastern North America, in the mint family, with small white flowers in whorls where the leaves meet the stem. This is the plant our listing names, and it is the name that governs this page.

cards.alt: The shop floor at 599 Smithdown Road, shelves along the wall
cards.p: Ask for bugle in a British garden and you get Ajuga reptans, a low creeping plant with blue flower spikes, in the same family and a different genus. Lycopus europaeus, gypsywort, gets called bugleweed too. Three plants, one English word, which is why the Latin is on the sheet.

cards.alt: Two plain capsules on a saucer beside a glass of water, a generated scene
cards.p: The parts above ground, cut when the plant is in flower, are what is normally milled under this name. Our listing says 100 per cent of the plant and does not say which part, so this page does not state one.

cards.alt: Plain capsules and a wooden scoop on a slate board, a generated scene
cards.p: The powder goes into a vegan capsule, with no filler and no bulking agent named on the listing. The shell material itself is not specified. These capsules are a generated scene rather than a photograph of ours.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The species is named in Latin and separated from the two other plants that share its English name. The serving and the price are printed. The count, the milligrams, the part used and the origin are printed as blanks, because that is what the listing gives us. What this plant does in a person is not something we are permitted to say, so it is not on this page.

reiss.label: From Reiss
reiss.h2: Three plants share this name, and one of them is in the jar
paras: If you ask for bugle in Britain you will be handed Ajuga reptans, the creeping thing with blue spikes that people grow at the front of a border. If you ask a herbalist in North America you will get Lycopus virginicus. There is a third, Lycopus europaeus, sold as gypsywort and sometimes as bugleweed. They are three different plants and only one of them is in this capsule.

Our listing names Lycopus virginicus, so that is what the sheet says and that is what any photograph on this page would have to be. There is no photograph of the plant here yet, because the one we were offered was the garden Ajuga, and a picture of the wrong plant is a worse mistake than no picture at all.

The rest of this label is thin. No count, no milligrams, no part named, no country. What it does carry is a caution, and that caution is printed above in the words the listing uses. Read it before the first capsule, and if any of it applies to you, ring the shop rather than guessing.
reiss.pull: A picture of the wrong plant is a worse mistake than no picture at all.
